page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine deployed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, configured with two dedicated virtual CPUs backed by one physical core with two threads. Operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz, the processor features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with support for AVX-512 vector extensions and hardware cryptographic routines. It is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio, but includes no local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate strong single-thread execution alongside aggregate throughput constrained by the small core footprint. In single-core stress-ng tests and compression benchmarks, the high CPU clock speed yields top-tier results, reaching 40.52 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 18.03 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-core throughput and overall PassMark CPU scores reflect the two-vCPU ceiling, categorizing multi-threaded stress and database operations within lower performance tiers. Memory performance remains balanced, recording large-block uncached read speeds of 43.28 GB/sec and write speeds of 33.7 GB/sec. The configuration delivers high memory density relative to core count, allowing memory-heavy small services to operate without paying for surplus compute capacity.

Given the 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, lack of ephemeral storage, and strong per-core instruction throughput, the E2as_v7 is structured for memory-intensive low-concurrency applications. Primary workloads include small in-memory caches, distributed database worker nodes, staging microservices, and lightweight data pre-processing jobs that require substantial working RAM without high parallel core scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure E2as_v7 is an entry-level memory-optimized instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, it allocates two dedicated virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with two threads. The configuration pairs 16.0 GB of memory with the dual-vCPU setup, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, while providing no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show exceptional single-core execution speed and top-tier compression throughput, complemented by steady uncached memory read and write bandwidths. However, multi-threaded capacity, overall PassMark compute scores, and static web serving throughput remain constrained by the low core count. The instance offers a resource-dense memory profile for workloads that prioritize RAM capacity over aggregate parallel computation, making it suitable for small in-memory caches, lightweight database nodes, and staging environments.
